journal_quotes: I began by leaving the model architecture unchanged, only changing hyperparameters by hand to understand their impacts.

We see that the baseline learning rate was perfect for this current configuration. All it truly needed was a few more epochs.
After my findings with accuracy revealed that the default learning rate was a solid starting point, I'm ready to move onto layers.

Right now I assume the issue is we're losing valuable signal as the layer layers add nothing but noise to an ultimately simple problem. I expect to see some small number of layers, perhaps 10-15 perform the same or better.
I expect to see some small number of layers, perhaps 10-15 perform the same or better.

Regression. Let's roll with 6 layers for now. Going to try a run with 50 epochs and 6 layers.
Zero change in the last epoch. Clearly reached the floor of this configuration.
My ideas here are to change the size of the residual stream (width) and the size of the hidden layers (hidden).
Perhaps a smaller residual stream is equally capable, perhaps a larger residual layer will allow more signal through.
Immediately slower training. Didn't reach 0.0# until epoch 18.
perhaps a larger residual layer will allow more signal through.
Incredible training accuracy but a trivial improvement in test. All we did was improve the models ability to overfit.
Let's try a 50 epoch here since I see a bit more room for training loss.
We gained an incredible -0.03%. I'd say that was just further overfitting pushing our performance worse.
For now, let's see what happens when we tinker with the size of the hidden layers. Perhaps reducing the models capacity will serve a similar role.
Crazy experiments over with no real change. This is obviously a dead end. Onto Regularization.
Weight decay is a classic from ML. Let's try to force down those worthless weights and see if we can open up some capacity for the test accuracy to use.
Didn't learn a thing.
Let's try suggestion from the internet, 1e-4.
This is interesting, we're almost back where we started but we still have a little wiggle room with train accuracy. I still see some more downward motion in the loss as well.
The plan paid off! We closed the train accuracy to 100% again and gained 0.10 of test accuracy.
Tried another jump in regularization and I'm starting to see a lot of oscillation. We've lost test accuracy in exchange for some train room.
We've lost test accuracy in exchange for some train room. Let me try a smaller learning rate.
a=0.03 worked. I saw oscillation happening and it predictably solved it.
With 0.01 we're seeing incredibly slow training with more room for training by epoch 50.
We're already using SGD, I have no interest in trying classical GD due to time and probable worse performance. So, let's try just adding some momentum and see what happens.
Well that didn't work. Let's try less.
Well that kinda worked. Maybe more regularization?
Huge overshoot. Let's try less momentum then bring in dampening. Could also try a smaller learning rate.
Doing something else as a waiting move. Changing weight decay back down and turning down batch size so it must generalize more.
Still oscillating.
https://distill.pub/2017/momentum/ This post opened my eyes. Let's experiment. Maybe our learning rate is too high? Let's try more momentum, less learning rate.
Slow training, okay results.

We will hopefully see some really nice improvements to accuracy and keep our weight decay to avoid overfitting. Turning down learning rate to match the lowerer needs of ADAMW as well.

At this point I added dropout to the output of the layer so it would have a 10% chance of setting a value of the input to zero.
Intuitively this makes sense. We randomly are tossing out information and asking the model to still answer the question.
